title: TileSetAtlasSource.create_tile() is O(n²) - large tilesets take tens of seconds to load
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf
- Present in source from at least 4.4-stable through 4.7-stable

### System information

Ubuntu 24.04.5 LTS - Intel Core i9-14900KF (32 threads), 62 GB RAM - Godot 4.7.2.stable, GL Compatibility, headless

### Issue description

**Human Foreword:** I had this issue dealing with a large tileset and had claude diagnose, find the fix then generate this ticket. Hope that doesn't count as AI slop-pyness but it is an actual issue was lagging the hell out of my game and the fix worked. I checked that it hadn't already been reported and it still exists in the current build.

Loading a large 16x16 tileset of about 56k tiles took about 43 seconds when running the game and brought the editor to a crawl, after trying different things it wasn't directly that there was a lot of tiles that was the problem, it was due to the godot code resorting every time a tile was initialized and added, splitting the same 56k tiles into separate sheets and then including all of them in the exact same board reduced load to about 1.3s. Problem isn't the large tile count, it's the way they're built internally.

Clanker probably wrote it up better below.

---

`TileSetAtlasSource::create_tile()` re-sorts the entire `tiles_ids` vector on every single insertion
(`scene/resources/2d/tile_set.cpp`, in 4.7-stable at line 5014):

```cpp
// Create and resize the tile.
tiles.insert(p_atlas_coords, tad);
tiles_ids.push_back(p_atlas_coords);
tiles_ids.sort();          // full re-sort, once per tile

_create_coords_mapping_cache(p_atlas_coords);
_queue_update_padded_texture();
```

with `Vector<Vector2i> tiles_ids;` declared in `scene/resources/2d/tile_set.h`.

Building a source of `n` tiles therefore costs `Σ k·log k ≈ (n²/2)·log₂ n` comparisons rather than a
single `O(n log n)` sort at the end. `remove_tile()` (line 5036) and `move_tile_in_atlas()` (line 5387)
re-sort the same way.

This is reached once per tile during resource loading. `TileSetAtlasSource::_set()` handles each
`"<x>:<y>/0"` property with:

```cpp
if (!has_tile(coords)) {
    create_tile(coords);
}
```

so a `.tres` defining `n` tiles pays the full quadratic cost on load.

The practical effect is that a tileset built from a large commercial atlas — the kind that ships as one
sheet of tens of thousands of 16×16 tiles — takes tens of seconds to load, and the same cost is paid
again on every edit in the TileSet editor. It is not obvious to users that tile *count* is the cause:
the natural suspects (texture size, VRAM, `use_texture_padding`, text vs. binary serialisation) are all
measurably irrelevant by comparison.

## Suggested fix

Sort lazily rather than eagerly. Replace the `tiles_ids.sort()` calls in `create_tile()`,
`remove_tile()` and `move_tile_in_atlas()` with a dirty flag, and sort on first read in the accessors
that depend on the ordering (`get_tile_id()`, and iteration over `tiles_ids`). That reduces bulk
construction from `O(n² log n)` to `O(n log n)` while leaving observable ordering unchanged.

A smaller change — `tiles_ids.ordered_insert()` in place of `push_back()` + `sort()` — keeps the vector
sorted at all times and cuts the constant factor substantially, but remains `O(n²)` because of the
element shifting.

## Workaround for users

Split the atlas across multiple `TileSetAtlasSource` entries, or multiple smaller tilesets. Per the
table above this gives close to an N× speedup for N sources, with no reduction in the number of tiles
available. Many commercial packs that ship a single merged sheet also ship the same art pre-split by
category; importing those instead is the least invasive route.


### Steps to reproduce

Self-contained, no external assets. Run with
`godot --headless --path <project> --script res://repro.gd`:

```gdscript
extends SceneTree


## Times TileSetAtlasSource.create_tile() as the tile count grows
func _initialize() -> void:
	for tile_target: int in [1000, 2000, 4000, 8000, 16000, 32000]:
		# Build an empty atlas source over a placeholder texture
		var texture := PlaceholderTexture2D.new()
		texture.size = Vector2(2816, 8224)
		var source := TileSetAtlasSource.new()
		source.texture = texture
		source.texture_region_size = Vector2i(16, 16)
		source.use_texture_padding = false

		# Create tiles one at a time, as the resource loader does
		var started_usec: int = Time.get_ticks_usec()
		var created: int = 0
		for y: int in 514:
			for x: int in 176:
				source.create_tile(Vector2i(x, y))
				created += 1
				if created >= tile_target:
					break
			if created >= tile_target:
				break
		var elapsed_usec: int = Time.get_ticks_usec() - started_usec

		print("%6d tiles: %8.3f s" % [created, elapsed_usec / 1000000.0])
	quit()
```

Observed:

| Tiles | Time | × previous |
|------:|------:|-----------:|
| 1,000 | 0.008 s | — |
| 2,000 | 0.036 s | 4.50 |
| 4,000 | 0.164 s | 4.55 |
| 8,000 | 0.714 s | 4.35 |
| 16,000 | 3.020 s | 4.23 |
| 32,000 | 12.632 s | 4.18 |

Each doubling of tile count roughly quadruples the time, as expected for `O(n²)`.

### Confirmation against a real tileset

A `TileSet` over a 2816×8224 atlas at 16×16, `use_texture_padding = false`, texture pre-warmed and
excluded from the measurement, loaded with `CACHE_MODE_IGNORE` in a fresh process (median of 3, or mean
of 2 above 16,000):

| Tiles | Load |
|------:|------:|
| 1,000 | 0.09 s |
| 4,000 | 0.27 s |
| 16,000 | 3.19 s |
| 32,000 | 13.19 s |
| 56,639 | **41.51 s** |

Fitting `t ≈ 1.228×10⁻⁵ n²` ms on the mid-range points predicts 12.6 s and 39.4 s for the last two rows
against measured 13.2 s and 41.5 s — within 5%.

Comparing the two tables at 32,000 tiles (12.63 s via the API, 13.19 s via a `.tres`) puts text parsing
at roughly 4% of load time. Serialising to binary `.res` does not measurably help, and neither does
`use_texture_padding = false`; both are dominated by this.

### The cost is per source, not per tileset

Splitting the identical 56,639 tiles across more `TileSetAtlasSource` entries in a single `TileSet`
over the same texture — every file below contains all 56,639 tiles, verified by summing
`get_tiles_count()` across sources:

| Sources | Tiles each | Load | Speedup |
|--------:|-----------:|------:|--------:|
| 1 | 56,639 | 41.51 s | — |
| 2 | 28,320 | 20.41 s | 2.03× |
| 4 | 14,160 | 10.03 s | 4.14× |
| 8 | 7,080 | 4.99 s | 8.32× |
| 16 | 3,540 | 2.54 s | 16.33× |
| 32 | 1,770 | 1.34 s | 31.06× |

The speedup is linear in the number of sources, consistent with `n²` cost accumulating independently
within each source's own `tiles_ids`.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

N/A - Single script in steps to reproduce above
